raw_text:
Below is a three-week reconditioning (deload-to-load transition) block designed to reintroduce training stimulus safely after a 3-week flu-related layoff. It emphasizes rebuilding tolerance, addressing movement quality, and reacclimating to heavy loading without reigniting fatigue. After this block, you can transition into a longer 6–9 week progressive strength phase targeting the same pre-illness targets (bench 100 kg, squat 140 kg, deadlift 170 kg).

Assumptions and context
- Client: 41-year-old male, intermediate lifter, full gym access.
- Pre-illness max-ish loads: bench ~100 kg, squat ~140 kg, deadlift ~170 kg.
- Current status: fatigue, ~4 kg weight loss, 3 weeks off.
- Goals: restore strength and movement quality, re-establish training tolerance, avoid overreaching.
- Training frequency: 4 days per week (can be adjusted to 3 if needed). Primary emphasis on: upper body pressing, lower body squats/deads, and total body posterior chain work.

Structure overview
- Week 1: Restore readiness, establish baseline, low-to-moderate intensity with higher reps to rebuild fatigue resistance. Emphasize technique, mobility, and conservative loading.
- Week 2: Gradual loading increase, introduce double-somite stimulus, start ramping weights toward but not exceeding rough pre-illness tolerance.
- Week 3: Rebuild tolerance with heavier sets at controlled RPE targets, approaching light-load peak for reintroduction to heavier strength work. By week’s end, feel ready to transition into a conventional 4–6 week strength block or a 6–8 week progression plan.

Programming notes
- Intensity: Use RPE and velocity cues. Target total weekly stress that remains below a personal fatigue ceiling; watch for lingering flu symptoms. If fatigue or symptoms worsen, scale back 10–15% and/or insert an extra rest day.
- RIR guidance: when not sure, err on the side of higher reps with higher RIR (8–9 RIR) in Week 1; move to 5–8 RIR in Week 2; aim for 2–4 RIR by Week 3 on heavier sets.
- Warm-up: Emphasize joint mobility and specific activation before main lifts (hips, ankles, thoracic spine; glutes, hamstrings, lats).
- Technique: Prioritize bar control, form, and depth for squats and benches; ensure deadlift setup is solid (hips, back, brace).
- Volume: Moderate; not pushing absolute maxes. The goal is to re-establish tolerances and movement quality, not to set new 1RM.

Week 1: Reconditioning and movement quality (4 sessions)
Mon — Upper Body Push + Mobility
- Warm-up: 10 minutes light cardio, dynamic shoulder/upper back work, banded pass-throughs, scapular push-ups.
- Bench Press: 4 sets x 8 reps @ RPE 6-7 (roughly 60–70% of old 1RM). Tempo controlled (2-0-1-0). Focus on bar path and leg drive.
- Incline Dumbbell Press: 3 sets x 10 reps @ RPE 6-7. Short rests, controlled tempo.
- Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press: 3 sets x 10 reps @ RPE 6-7.
- Triceps accessories: Rope Pushdowns 3 x 12, Dumbbell Skull Crushers 2 x 12.
- Core: Plank 3 x 30–45 seconds; dead bug 2 x 12 per side.
- Mobility/cool-down: chest/lat stretches, upper thoracic mobility 5–8 minutes.

Tue — Lower Body foundational (posterior chain emphasis)
- Warm-up: 5–8 minutes bike/row, dynamic leg swings, hip circles.
- Back Squat: 4 sets x 8 reps @ RPE 6–7 (roughly 60–70% of prior 1RM). Focus on depth and brace.
- Romanian Deadlift (Romanian or paused): 3 sets x 10 reps @ RPE 6–7. Emphasize hamstrings and glutes, keep back neutral.
- Front/Goblet Squats: 2 sets x 12 reps @ light load to reinforce depth and position.
- Leg Curl (machine) 3 x 12; Calf Raises 3 x 15.
- Mobility/Recovery: hip flexor stretch, hamstring stretch 20–30s each; foam roll as tolerated.

Thu — Upper Body Pull + Stability
- Warm-up: 5–8 minutes cardio; banded pull-aparts, face pulls, thoracic mobility.
- Barbell Rows or Dumbbell Rows: 4 sets x 8–10 reps @ RPE 6–7.
- Lat Pulldown or Pull-ups (assisted if needed): 3 sets x 8–10 reps @ RPE 6–7.
- Seated Cable Rows: 3 x 12
- Bicep Curls: 2 x 12
- Core: Pallof press 3 x 12 per side; farmer’s carry 2 x 30 seconds if comfortable.
- Mobility/Recovery: posterior chain mobility, lat stretch.

Fri — Full Body with light loading and movement quality
- Warm-up: 5–10 minutes light cardio; mobility work.
- Deadlift (or trap bar deadlift) Medium Set: 3 sets x 6–8 reps @ RPE 7.
- Dumbbell Lunges or Split Squat: 3 sets x 10 reps per leg @ RPE 6–7.
- Overhead Press (light): 2–3 sets x 10 reps @ RPE 6-7
- Yoke carry / Suitcase carry or, if unavailable, rear foot elevated glute bridge: 2 x 30 seconds
- Core: side planks 2 x 30s per side
- Mobility/Recovery: hip flexor, piriformis stretch, thoracic mobility.

Notes for Week 1
- Focus on form; no failure.
- Keep training stress moderate; prioritize consistency.
- Sleep 7–9 hours, maintain hydration, and ensure adequate protein intake (approx 1.6–2.0 g/kg bodyweight, depending on appetite).

Week 2: Progressive loading and controlled ramp (4 sessions)
Mon — Bench pressing and upper body density
- Warm-up: mobility, shoulder prehab (banded dislocations, face pulls).
- Bench Press: 4 sets x 6–8 reps @ RPE 7 (60–75% of pre-illness 1RM; if not confident, keep reps at 6).
- Overhead Press: 3 sets x 8 reps @ RPE 7.
- Close-Grip Bench or Floor Press: 3 x 8 @ RPE 7.
- Triceps: Rope Pushdowns 3 x 12
- Core: Weighted carries 2 x 30 seconds
- Mobility: thoracic spine rotation, pec stretch.

Tue — Lower body – volume build with emphasis on technique
- Warm-up: dynamic hamstring/hip prep.
- Squat: 4 sets x 6–8 reps @ RPE 7 (increase load modestly from Week 1; aim for 65–75% of pre-illness).
- Front Squats or Zercher (light): 3 x 6–8 @ RPE 7.
- Romanian Deadlift: 3 x 8–10 @ RPE 7
- Leg Curl: 3 x 10–12
- Calves: 3 x 12–15
- Mobility/Recovery: hip and ankle mobility.

Thu — Upper Pull and Stability
- Warm-up: banded rows, shoulder prehab.
- Barbell Row: 4 x 8 @ RPE 7
- Lat Pulldown: 3 x 8–10 @ RPE 7
- Seated Dumbbell Curl 2 x 12
- Face Pulls: 3 x 15
- Core: AB wheel or dead bug 3 x 12
- Mobility: thoracic mobility, lats stretch.

Fri — Full body and density work
- Deadlift: 3–4 sets x 5 reps @ RPE 7 (conservative; consider using mixed grip and strap if needed; avoid max effort)
- Split Squat or step-ups: 3 x 8 per leg
- Dumbbell Bench Press or Push-ups: 3 x 12
- Back Extension or Glute Bridge: 3 x 12–15
- Farmer’s Carry: 2 x 40 seconds
- Core: Pallof press 3 x 12 per side
- Mobility/Recovery: light.

Week 3: Higher load tolerance and preparation for heavier loads (4 sessions)
Mon — Bench-focused strength reintroduction
- Warm-up: active shoulder/upper back prep.
- Bench Press: 5 sets x 5 reps @ RPE 7–8 (target around 75–85% of pre-illness 1RM if tolerating; otherwise stay at 6–8 reps with RPE 7)
- Incline Dumbbell Press: 3 sets x 6–8 @ RPE 7
- Dips or Push-ups: 3 x 8–10
- Triceps: Cable Pushdowns 3 x 12
- Core: Hanging leg raises 3 x 8–10
- Mobility: quick chest/shoulder stretch.

Tue — Lower body – posterior chain emphasis and strength cues
- Warm-up: hip hinge, ankle mobility
- Back Squat: 5 x 5 @ RPE 7–8 (aim for 75–85% if tolerating)
- Romanian Deadlift: 4 x 6–8 @ RPE 7–8
- Lunges or Bulgarian Split Squats: 3 x 8 per leg
- Leg Curl: 3 x 8–10
- Calf Raises: 3 x 12–15
- Core: suitcase carries 2 x 30 seconds per side
- Mobility/Recovery: posterior chain focus.

Thu — Upper Pull + Light Power Endpoints
- Warm-up: scapular activation
- Barbell Row: 4 x 6–8 @ RPE 7–8
- Pull-ups/Lat Pulldown: 4 x 6–8 @ RPE 7
- Dumbbell Shrugs: 3 x 10–12
- Bicep Curls 2 x 12
- Core: ab wheel 2 x 8–10
- Mobility: thoracic mobility.

Fri — Full body integration and density
- Deadlift or Trap Bar Deadlift: 4 x 4–6 @ RPE 7–8 (tolerating; not max)
- Front Squat or Goblet Squat: 3 x 6–8 @ RPE 7
- Dumbbell Bench Press or Barbell Overhead Press: 3 x 8–10
- Hip Thrust or Glute Bridge: 3 x 10–12
- Farmers Carry: 2 x 40–60 seconds
- Core: side planks 3 x 30–45 seconds per side
- Mobility/Recovery: deep breathing, mobility.

Assessment and progression guidance
- Week 3 is a bridge to a conventional 4–6 week strength block. If progression stalls due to remaining fatigue, reduce loading by 5–10% and maintain volume with better technique.
- If the client experiences persistent fever, fatigue, or flu-like symptoms, reduce volume further and consider adding a fourth rest day or moving to a 3x/week model temporarily.

Nutrition and recovery guidance
- Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg body weight per day to support recovery and lean mass regain.
- Calorie intake: aim for a small surplus or maintenance if weight loss continues; initial target around maintenance or slight surplus (100–300 kcal/day) to regain weight and energy.
- Hydration: 2.5–3.5 L/day (adjust to thirst and climate).
- Sleep: 7–9 hours per night; prioritize consistent sleep patterns.
- Vitamin D, omega-3s, and a multivitamin may help general recovery if dietary intake is insufficient.
- Recovery modalities: consider 1–2 short mobility sessions on off days, light walking, or easy cycling; gentle massage or foam rolling.

Monitoring and red flags
- Watch for symptoms such as excessive fatigue, fever, chest pain, dizziness, or lightheadedness during sessions. If these occur, stop, reassess and consult a clinician as needed.
- Track RPE, soreness, and sleep. If soreness remains high for several days, dial back intensity or volume by 20–30%.

Transition plan after week 3
- Re-evaluate progress with a simple performance check: bench 90–95% of pre-illness feel, squat around 85–95% if tolerated, deadlift around 90–95% if tolerated, across sets with proper form.
- Move into a 4–6 week strength block focusing on gradually increasing working sets at 2–4% weekly progression while preserving technique and recovery.
- Consider re-establishing 1RM targets only after volume and load tolerances have been consistently met for 2–3 weeks.

If you want, I can tailor this plan further to match exact weekly workout days, equipment availability, or preferred exercise substitutions, or convert it into a day-by-day CSV for your client management system.
